STORY SO FAR: Tue 07-28 — a DEEP-DIVE, learner-commissioned: Andrew asked for pakkam vs paakkalaam by name on 07-27 and it was paid off first, before any demand. THE HEADLINE IS A METHOD CHANGE, not a word: the minimal pair EXPLAINS the collision and does not FIRE it. I gave the full contrast (paar hiding inside paakkalaam, paarthen already his, long aa + the r vs pakkam's two flat beats) and ninety seconds later, under production load, he still said 'temple-ku pakkalam' — told the driver 'let us go look at a temple' for the second day running. What fixed it inside ONE exchange was dropping the pair and handing pakkathula as an INDIVISIBLE CHUNK — 'nothing to build, learn it like paravaayilla'. The diagnosis: while he is assembling pakkam + -la, the worn groove -alaam gets out of his mouth first. Assembly loses to retrieval under load. Apply this shape to every minimal pair from here — contrast to explain, chunk to fire.
